text:
St. Louis arrives at Madison Square Garden in better shape than New York. The Blues beat Detroit 5-4 on Friday after trailing by two goals, with Aleksanteri Kaskimaki scoring his first NHL goal, and they are 3-2-0 in their last five. They are still missing Ross Johnston and Dillon Dube. The Rangers have lost four straight (0-4-0) and are 1-4-0 over their last five, most recently 4-1 to Edmonton on Sunday. They are also without goalie Igor Shesterkin, who is on injured reserve, and defenseman Sean Durzi is day-to-day and could return.

Our numbers see very little separating the teams. Each has taken about half the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five, and our model has the game at 2.98 to 2.96 in St. Louis's favor. The Rangers' power play creates more (0.64 expected goals a game to 0.47), but they take four penalties a game, which keeps giving opponents chances. In net, projected starter Joel Hofer is 2.9 goals saved above expected this season and was 11.1 over 46 games last year. New York's projected Dylan Garand sits at -0.4 after 11 games.

Pavel Dorofeyev is on a five-game point streak, and as the New York Post noted, Mike Sullivan has shaken up the lineup to get him going. He has a 32% chance to score. Alexis Lafreniere, the first overall pick in 2020, is at 31%. For the Blues, Jimmy Snuggerud has seven goals and nine points in his last ten, but our numbers say bounces drove much of it, so expect him to cool. Mason McTavish, pointless in four on 2.6 expected goals, is due.
